## Simple explanation

TensorFlow is a software platform for creating and running machine-learning
models. It provides numerical operations, automatic differentiation,
training tools, and deployment options across different devices.

## Technical explanation

TensorFlow provides tensor operations and automatic gradient computation,
with higher-level APIs such as Keras for model construction and training.
Its ecosystem includes tools for data input, distributed execution,
conversion, and deployment.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

TensorFlow is used to develop and deploy models in research and production.
Its APIs and deployment ecosystem support workflows from experimentation
to mobile and server environments, though teams should select tools that
fit their model and operational constraints.

## How it works

Developers define a model and loss, provide data, and use an optimizer to
update trainable variables from computed gradients. TensorFlow can execute
operations on supported hardware and export models for compatible
deployment runtimes.

## Practical example

A classification model can be built with Keras layers, trained on batches
of labeled examples, and evaluated on held-out data. The exported model
should be tested in the same runtime and input format used in deployment.

## Common misconceptions

- TensorFlow is a framework, not a model or a guarantee of good predictions.
- An exported model still depends on compatible operators, preprocessing,
  and runtime configuration.
